hoe.name: Hoe
hoe.desc: Till soil so seeds can be planted. Tilling breaks up soil crumbs, so till only where you'll plant.

can.name: Watering Can
can.desc: Water tilled soil. Refill at the pond or a rain barrel.

scythe.name: Scythe
scythe.desc: Cut weeds. You get plant fiber for the compost bin.

axe.name: Axe
axe.desc: Chop sticks, logs, stumps, and trees into wood. Bigger things take more swings.

pickaxe.name: Pickaxe
pickaxe.desc: Break stones. Also un-tills a tile.

shovel.name: Shovel
shovel.desc: Dig a test hole: reveals soil life and structure (the shovel test).

ring.name: Infiltration Ring
ring.desc: Time how fast water soaks in: reveals water holding.

axe_copper.name: Copper Axe
axe_copper.desc: Breaks trees, logs, and stumps 2× as fast as a basic axe. Lasts about 120 uses.

pickaxe_copper.name: Copper Pickaxe
pickaxe_copper.desc: Breaks stones and ore 2× as fast as a basic pickaxe. Lasts about 120 uses.

axe_bronze.name: Bronze Axe
axe_bronze.desc: Breaks trees, logs, and stumps 3× as fast as a basic axe. Lasts about 180 uses.

pickaxe_bronze.name: Bronze Pickaxe
pickaxe_bronze.desc: Breaks stones and ore 3× as fast as a basic pickaxe. Lasts about 180 uses.

axe_iron.name: Iron Axe
axe_iron.desc: Breaks trees, logs, and stumps 4× as fast as a basic axe. Lasts about 260 uses.

pickaxe_iron.name: Iron Pickaxe
pickaxe_iron.desc: Breaks stones and ore 4× as fast as a basic pickaxe. Lasts about 260 uses.

axe_gold.name: Gold Axe
axe_gold.desc: Breaks trees, logs, and stumps 6× as fast as a basic axe. Lasts about 90 uses. Gold is soft, so it wears out fast.

pickaxe_gold.name: Gold Pickaxe
pickaxe_gold.desc: Breaks stones and ore 6× as fast as a basic pickaxe. Lasts about 90 uses. Gold is soft, so it wears out fast.

axe_mithril.name: Mithril Axe
axe_mithril.desc: Breaks trees, logs, and stumps 8× as fast as a basic axe. Lasts about 500 uses.

pickaxe_mithril.name: Mithril Pickaxe
pickaxe_mithril.desc: Breaks stones and ore 8× as fast as a basic pickaxe. Lasts about 500 uses.

labKit.name: Lab Test Kit
labKit.desc: Mail a sample to the lab: reveals organic matter, nutrients, and pH.

compost.name: Compost
compost.desc: Adds organic matter, soil life, and slow-release nutrients.

mulch.name: Straw Mulch
mulch.desc: Covers soil: keeps moisture in, blocks weeds, protects from storms.

lime.name: Garden Lime
lime.desc: Ground limestone. Raises pH in acidic soil.

biochar.name: Biochar
biochar.desc: Charcoal full of tiny pores. Permanently helps soil hold water and nutrients.

synthFert.name: Synthetic Fertilizer
synthFert.desc: Fast nutrients, but not organic: using it ends your organic certification, and extra washes away.

fiber.name: Plant Fiber
fiber.desc: From weeds. Feed it to a compost bin.

honey.name: Honey
honey.desc: Made by bees from flower nectar.

egg.name: Egg
egg.desc: Fresh from your hens, who eat bugs and weed seeds all day.

sticks.name: Sticks
sticks.desc: Split from wood at a workbench. Handles for tools.

refinedFiber.name: Refined Fiber
refinedFiber.desc: Plant fiber spun smooth and strong on a spinning wheel.

rope.name: Rope
rope.desc: Refined fiber twisted into rope. Lashes tool heads to handles.

copperBar.name: Copper Bar
copperBar.desc: Smelted from copper ore. Makes copper tools.

bronzeBar.name: Bronze Bar
bronzeBar.desc: An alloy of copper and tin, harder than either one alone.

ironBar.name: Iron Bar
ironBar.desc: Smelted from iron ore. Tough and long-lasting.

goldBar.name: Gold Bar
goldBar.desc: Pure gold. Beautiful, valuable, and soft.

mithrilBar.name: Mithril Bar
mithrilBar.desc: Glows faintly blue. The best tools are made from it.

copperOre.name: Copper Ore
copperOre.desc: Green-streaked rock with copper in it. Found near the top of the mine.

tinOre.name: Tin Ore
tinOre.desc: Heavy, dark rock with tin in it. Melt it with copper to make bronze.

ironOre.name: Iron Ore
ironOre.desc: Rusty red rock full of iron. Found from floor 5 down.

goldOre.name: Gold Ore
goldOre.desc: Quartz with flecks of real gold. Found from floor 10 down.

mithrilOre.name: Mithril Ore
mithrilOre.desc: A glowing blue ore from the deepest floors. (Mithril comes from stories, not real geology.)

kit_composter.name: Compost Bin
kit_composter.desc: Add 5 plant fiber; decomposers turn it into compost in 2 days.

kit_rainBarrel.name: Rain Barrel
kit_rainBarrel.desc: Catches rainwater to refill your watering can.

kit_beehive.name: Beehive
kit_beehive.desc: Bees pollinate nearby crops and make honey when flowers are close.

kit_birdHouse.name: Bird House
kit_birdHouse.desc: Birds eat caterpillars and other pests nearby.

kit_bugHotel.name: Bug Hotel
kit_bugHotel.desc: A home for ladybugs and other helpful insects that eat aphids.

kit_scarecrow.name: Scarecrow
kit_scarecrow.desc: Keeps crows from eating seedlings nearby.

kit_greenhouse.name: Greenhouse
kit_greenhouse.desc: Glass traps the sun's heat. Grow any crop in any season inside!

kit_pathStone.name: Stepping Stone
kit_pathStone.desc: A path tile. Walk on it, don't till it.

kit_well.name: Well
kit_well.desc: Reaches groundwater. Refill your watering can here any time.

kit_chickenCoop.name: Chicken Coop
kit_chickenCoop.desc: Hens lay eggs every morning, eat pests on nearby crops, and their manure becomes compost.

kit_workbench.name: Workbench
kit_workbench.desc: Craft sticks, chests, and the other workstations.

kit_grinder.name: Grinder
kit_grinder.desc: Sharpen and fit tool heads: makes axes, pickaxes, and other tools.

kit_spinningWheel.name: Spinning Wheel
kit_spinningWheel.desc: Spin plant fiber into refined fiber, and refined fiber into rope.

kit_furnace.name: Furnace
kit_furnace.desc: Smelts ore into metal bars, burning wood for heat.

kit_chest.name: Storage Chest
kit_chest.desc: Twenty slots of storage. Put it anywhere on your farm.

kit_smallBarn.name: Small Barn
kit_smallBarn.desc: Stores hay. Old hay becomes straw mulch you can collect each morning.

seed_clover.name: Clover Seeds
seed_clover.desc: Cool-season crop, 60 days on the seed packet. Takes: Almost nothing. It's grown to feed the soil, not to sell. Gives back: A cover crop: roots hold the soil, root nodules add nitrogen, and digging it in (green manure) adds organic matter.

seed_beans.name: Bean Seeds
seed_beans.desc: Warm-season crop, 55 days on the seed packet, keeps producing. Takes: Very little. Beans make their own nitrogen. Gives back: Adds nitrogen! Bacteria in little root bumps (nodules) pull nitrogen from the air into the soil.

seed_buckwheat.name: Buckwheat Seeds
seed_buckwheat.desc: Warm-season crop, 70 days on the seed packet. Takes: Very little. Grows well in poor soil. Gives back: Grows so fast it smothers weeds, unlocks phosphorus for the next crop, and adds organic matter.

seed_carrot.name: Carrot Seeds
seed_carrot.desc: Cool-season crop, 70 days on the seed packet. Takes: A light feeder. Needs a little potassium. Gives back: Long taproots push through packed soil and leave channels for air and water.

seed_wheat.name: Wheat Seeds
seed_wheat.desc: Cool-season crop, 100 days on the seed packet. Takes: Some nitrogen. Gives back: Straw left on the field adds organic matter, and a mat of fine roots holds soil in place.

seed_potato.name: Seed Potatoes
seed_potato.desc: Cool-season crop, 90 days on the seed packet. Takes: Uses lots of potassium to grow big tubers. Gives back: Nothing. Digging up the potatoes breaks apart soil crumbs.

seed_sunflower.name: Sunflower Seeds
seed_sunflower.desc: Warm-season crop, 80 days on the seed packet. Takes: A light feeder. Gives back: Deep taproots break up hard layers and pull up nutrients from deep down. Bees love them.

seed_squash.name: Squash Seeds
seed_squash.desc: Warm-season crop, 100 days on the seed packet. Takes: A medium feeder. Gives back: Giant leaves shade the ground like a living mulch: fewer weeds and less erosion.

seed_corn.name: Corn Seeds
seed_corn.desc: Warm-season crop, 80 days on the seed packet. Takes: A heavy feeder. Pulls lots of nitrogen out of the soil. Gives back: Stalks and roots left behind add a little organic matter.

seed_tomato.name: Tomato Seeds
seed_tomato.desc: Warm-season crop, 80 days on the seed packet, keeps producing. Takes: A heavy feeder. Needs lots of nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and calcium. Gives back: Not much for the soil, but tomatoes sell for the most.
